text: Project Zomboid can be a very difficult game if you're inexperienced.
So today I'm bringing you all the tips and tricks to become a superhuman survivor.
That way you'll live long enough to be the last of us.
Starting it up from beginner to advanced.
A lot of which you might not have known, but if I missed any feel free to leave it in the comments.
Let's get it rocking.
When you spawn, if you stay close to your spawn location, there's a higher chance for less zombies.
So always search around your spawn location first.
You can visit the Project Zomboid Map Project website to get a full map to check your location.
The best place to find starter weapons are kitchens, bathrooms, closets, and garages.
If you think it can be used as a weapon, it probably can be.
The main essential items to grab first are a weapon, water bottle, backpack, can opener, and a watch.
The main tools, a hammer and a saw, are a bonus.
Any container that you think could hold water probably will.
So don't be afraid to pour out a bleach bottle and fill it back up with water, or even use a bowl.
Any item with fresh water in your main inventory, your character will drink from automatically.
So this will cover your thirst.
Just remember to fill it back up frequently.
Cook any raw foods in a microwave, stove, or campfire to avoid getting sick.
But watch it closely so it doesn't burn, also making you sick.
Be sure to turn off the appliance so it doesn't catch fire.
Avoid eating rotten or stale foods also.
When fighting more than one zombie, kite backwards while swinging.
But don't forget you can point and shove if one gets too close.
As long as you aren't exhausted, you can outwalk the zombies and even swing, walk, swing, walk.
But make sure you have enough time for your character to turn.
Also hold your aiming beacon further out in the direction you want to swing.
Don't hold it too close to your character.
And 360 often in aim mode to check the surrounding area in your backside so you don't get snuck up on.
Smacking zombies also creates a lot of noise, and you can attract more.
Your weapons can also break, so keep a backup.
Some weapons can be repaired with duct tape or glue.
Avoid jogging or sprinting at all costs, as it will quickly exhaust your character and you can even trip and fall.
Too many weapon swings will also exhaust your character, so take it easy on fighting big hordes.
You'd be surprised where you can find certain loot items, so check everything.
But be careful how much you carry early on.
Try for only the essentials and running back loot to a safe spot.
You can literally just throw it on the ground.
Being too heavy will exhaust you quickly and when you're exhausted you move slower, putting you in danger and affecting your combat.
The tired moodle will also affect this, so rest up and avoid combat.
You can also carry heavy items in your secondary, lessening the weight to avoid exhaustion.
Put items in your backpack to reduce the weight also.
Zombies chase by last known location with sight and sound.
So crouching can sneak around them, or be used with building corners to give them the slip.
The best bandages are ripped sheets, and can be acquired by ripping up pillowcases, clothes, or even curtains.
If you run into locked doors and windows, you can smash down doors or bust out windows.
The larger weapons will knock down doors faster, and make sure a weapon is in your hand to
Bust out windows or you'll use your arm and cut yourself.
Don't forget to remove the broken glass also.
Leather jackets are a gift from God.
Protecting you from rain, preventing your player from catching a cold, and also giving you more protection against bites and scratches from the zombies.
Always wear one, it'll save your life.
Inside buildings, be prepared at all times.
Drawing your weapon up by holding right click, assume every corner and door is hiding a zombie, and always be prepared going up or down stairs.
If you're unsure of what's behind a door, you can aim and shove it with the spacebar to create noise, aggroing any zombies inside,
And they'll begin banging at the door.
Zombies can see and hear you through windows and doors.
You can either close the curtains if present, or use a sheet for a makeshift one.
The TV on the Life and Living channel has many shows to give you experience for your skills.
Every day around noon, the Woodcraft show will come on, and catching it will give you a massive
Boost to your carpentry skills, allowing you to build items like rain barrels.
The TV programming only runs for the first week, so be sure to catch it.
Reading the associated books takes time, but will give you a 100% experience buff to that skill.
You can also find the TV show VHS tapes to be played at any time, inserting it into a TV.
Don't forget about recipe magazines.
The best places to find books and magazines are on bookshelves, but you can also find them in certain vehicles, cardboard boxes, magazine racks,
And even mailboxes.
When it comes to barricading windows and doors, metal barricades require a blowtorch, welding mask, and large sheets.
No skill is required, but they actually have less health than the wood barricades when carpentry skill has been leveled.
If you haven't found an axe or nails, you can dismantle furniture using a saw and hammer to get those planks and nails.
Try to base up around high fences as zombies can't climb over them, protecting you from migrating hordes during meta events.
You can jump these fences by pressing the E key, but make sure you're not exhausted or heavy or you'll fail.
Hop low fences with E as well, but never jog or sprint over them, as there's a chance to trip, injuring yourself or dropping your weapon.
The power and water will randomly shut off during the first 30 days.
You can still get a little bit of water from sinks, bathtubs, and toilets afterwards, but it's limited.
You can prepare for this by collecting rainwater with random containers or by building rain barrels.
Make sure to boil that water though.
The game will let you know if a container you filled is tainted.
You can pick up and move most objects and even use some as barricades blocking entrances.
Make sure to put a few around windows because the first object becomes phantom, allowing the player or zombies to walk through it.
Car keys are located in the glove box, ignition, on the ground around the car, on nearby zombies, or in nearby containers inside buildings.
It probably won't have gas, but you can use any container with a lid to siphon some, like bleach bottles or water bottles.
Some vehicles and garages can also contain a gas can, so check those trunks.
If a trunk is locked, enter the vehicle and locate the unlock on the dash.
Be sure to put car keys on your key ring, and when inserting the key into the ignition, be sure to grab it again
When leaving and turning the car off.
Headlights will drain a car's battery, so remember that as well.
You can also level Mechanics to level 2 and Electrical to level 1 to hotwire cars.
Take apart electronics including digital watches to level Electrical.
Take car windows in and out, take the lights in and out, or take the tires on and off to level Mechanics.
The first two take a screwdriver, but tires will require a jack and a lug wrench.
When you hotwire a car, it requires a screwdriver as well.
Vehicle conditions are important because if the conditions of certain parts are too low, the car will randomly die,
Which can put you in a dicey situation.
Or the car may take many more tries to start, also putting you in danger.
If zombies approach the car, you can use the V key to switch seats and jump out the other side.
You can also roll down the passenger window to cool the car off on hot days.
Never roll down the driver's.
If breaking into a car for hotwiring or looting, also break out the passenger window.
You can access vehicle options with the V key for things like checking for gas to siphon, busting
Out a window, switching seats, or filling it up at the pumps.
Never be outside at night unless you have to, because your view becomes much smaller and it's difficult to see the zombies.
But if you are, a flashlight can be turned on and off with the F key.
This will drain the battery, but you can replace it with more you find by removing them from electronics like radios.
Should you ever get injured, check it immediately on the character health panel.
This will show you how fast you're bleeding and the type, plus location of the wound.
Scratches can just be bandaged, but lacerations and deep wounds need to be stitched before bandaging.
You can do this by locating a needle and thread from a sewing kit, or sometimes a suture needle from ambulances or medical supply cabinets.
You can sometimes get thread from ripping up clothing, but a suture needle requires no thread and is a one-time use item.
Don't even worry about changing bandages should they become soiled.
Let them ride.
But keep an eye on it and be prepared should it get infected.
You can use antibiotics or disinfectant, bourbon, or alcohol wipes to clean the wound and re-bandage.
Avoid falling from great heights as you can break your legs or even kill your character.
But you can jump out a second story window as long as you aren't too heavy with loot.
The helicopter event will happen between days 6 to 9 randomly.
You can prepare by barricading yourself in and clearing the nearby area of zombies.
The second story is a safer location.
If you're outside and the chopper sees you, it will stay longer and make more passes.
If inside, it'll do less.
But you can also just bail out in a car, but be sure to take it away from your base.
Walk if you have to.
Car doors are not broken in the game as some have stated.
When you enter a car, if you press the gas too quickly, the car door will not shut properly.
You can tell this by the sound it makes.
If it shuts properly, there's more of a thunk to the sound.
So always pay attention so you're not grabbed and bitten by an open car door going down the road.
When walking through trees, you can be scratched by them, so right click and use the Walk To feature to guide your character through safely.
You can also use it when building rooftops to avoid falling.
You can use campfires or molotovs to burn down hordes, but be careful, you can burn yourself, too.
If there's smoke, there's a chance for fire, so be careful walking when burning them down.
The smaller flames will turn into larger ones when the fire rages.
You can make a molotov with a bottle of bourbon or filling a glass bottle with gasoline.
Use a ripped sheet for the wick and it requires a lighter to start before throwing.
Campfires and antique stoves you can light by making a notched plank and sturdy stick.
This requires a saw and a screwdriver or knife to make though.
The best places to locate lighters are glove boxes, on zombies, or in gas station shelves.
If you spot a zombie with a clothing item you want, be sure to use a blunt weapon as it won't damage the article of clothing.
Bladed weapons will.
Sometimes you can find dope helmets on zombies also.
Survivor zombies and houses are some of the best places to get loot as they have a high chance for rare weapons like axes and machetes.
They will almost always have zombies inside though, so be careful.
You can use a claw hammer or a crowbar to remove the barricades, or just aggro the zombies and wait for them to break out.
There's a chance for burned down houses.
The fireman zombies or trucks can have fire axes, the best tool for knocking down garage doors.
They also have fireman suits, which are the warmest and most protective clothing.
Random construction trucks have a high chance for great loot like tools, including the sledgehammer
Which you can use to destroy all objects in the game including stairs.
There's also a high chance for the sledge on metal shelves or warehouse crates.
Be sure to check those garages.
The best weapons in Apocalypse mode are actually the hammer and the pipe wrench.
You can only hit one zombie at a time, but they are the most durable one-handed weapons that won't exhaust your character from using two hands.
You can only hit one zombie at a time in Apocalypse mode anyway.
But these have good knockdown power and the hammer four-hit quits the higher zombie health.
Generators are best found in garages, sheds, and self-storage.
They are incredibly heavy, but you can still put them in the passenger seats of cars even though it's red.
You'll need the How to Use Generators magazine to operate them and some gasoline to run them.
Over time, you'll need electronic scraps to repair them or they can explode, burning down your base.
You can acquire electronic scraps by dismantling electronics including watches or radios from cars.
When it comes to planting crops, you can use a hand fork, sometimes located on zombies, a trowel, or any shovel to dig furrows.
Cabbages and potatoes are the best to plant.
Cabbages take 10 days to grow while potatoes take 20.
But potatoes will last the longest before rotting.
If you lack a freezer, fridge, or generator, you can plant a tile every two days to prolong them.
Also, planting a tile apart will prevent disease from spreading between the plants.
Don't forget you can tow cars.
Set a watch alarm to maintain a sleep schedule.
Read books, magazines, and watch TV shows to improve your mood.
And use toilet paper or tissues to muffle your coughs and sneezes, should you catch a cold.
A good warm night's sleep on a full stomach will alleviate the cold.
You can plumb sinks to rain barrels on the roof to remove the need to boil water.
This does require a pipe wrench to be able to do.
Meta events, which are in-game sounds, migrate the zombies around should they hear it.
So always pay attention to this.
It could be a gunshot, screams, or even wolves howling.
When it comes to fishing, you'll need the magazines to make fishing poles or repair them, should you find them as loot.
Dig furrows to get worms as bait or forage up insects.
If you find tackle, that's pretty good also, but has a higher chance to catch junk items like shoes or break your line and pole.
Spear fishing is useless until you reach higher fishing levels, taking too long to catch at lower levels.
Foraging is an incredibly useful feature as you can do it anywhere and different environments contain different chances for loot.
Urban areas have the best chance for random items including most in the game,
While vegetation and forest areas have the best chance for food, bait, and crafting materials.
Don't forget that you can craft hammers, axes, and knives with sticks and stones found from foraging.
If you can't find a place to sleep for the night, you can sleep in cars.
But there's a chance for zombies coming up to the windows.
You can actually park the driver's window up against an object, preventing the zombies from accessing it.
The best way to tackle larger hordes are with molotovs, guns, or chipping away at them, crouching
And alerting a couple at a time, drawing them away.
Guns are pretty useless early game as it takes a high aiming and reloading level to be effective.
They draw in tons of zombies from the sound and it'll take a lot of ammunition.
The best way to level aiming is to use a shotgun and circle the horde firing into it.
Keep in mind though that it takes about 1,000 rounds to reach level 5 aiming.
You can also fire a gun from a vehicle through a rolled down window.
Should your gun jam, press the X button to rack it.
You can open doors from behind you by pressing E, so if you're fighting, kiting backwards, you can back out of a house.
Too many dead bodies around can give you corpse sickness, so avoid prolonged exposure.
Be sure to wash your character on a regular basis to avoid wound infection or contracting the zomboid virus by being covered in zombie blood.
All types of soap will speed up this process.
The best way to level Carpentry is by dismantling beds, as they give the highest experience per item.
For Metalworking, it's burnt down car wrecks.
You can refill a propane torch with a tank found in crates or barbecue grills.
For Electrical, it's radios, as they are the most plentiful.
Don't worry about Tailoring or First Aid.
All other skills are just by completing the actions.
Strength and Nimble are the most important combat skills, as Strength gives you more damage
And knockdown power while Nimble allows you to walk backwards in aim mode faster.
You can level Strength by exercising, and Nimble just by walking in aim mode.
Vehicle gas consumption is based off of RPMs, and the sound level produced is also by vehicle condition and RPMs.
You can mitigate this by tapping the gas, keeping your RPMs low after the vehicle shifts.
It takes a little practice, but is incredibly effective.
Tire pressure affects how well the car rolls, and you should keep your speeds low to prevent tire wear, crashing, or rolling the vehicle.
If you use your car to mush down zombies, the panels will damage to zero eventually and it will start damaging the parts, causing a breakdown.
Also avoid tire blowouts.
Remember that long-term survival is based off of avoiding injury, overwhelming or surprising zombies, and ensuring you have long-term food, water, shelter, and weapons covered.
Take good care of your character and think about how everything affects them.
Treat them as a real person.
This game is pretty much a simulator.
